dedupe_keys.name: long term monitoring of stormwater runoff and water quality in urbanized watersheds of the greater phoenix metropolitan area ongoing since 2008

description: This CAP LTER data package records stormwater runoff and water quality in urbanised catchments of the Phoenix metropolitan area. Arizona State University researchers and collaborators began monitoring in 2008 to study how urban land use and drainage infrastructure affect water and material flows. Version 6, published in July 2026, lists runoff chemistry, discharge, particulate measurements, an analyte table and Indian Bend Wash catchment geometry. Coverage includes the Indian Bend Wash in Scottsdale and Salt River subcatchments. Automated samplers collect discrete observations through runoff-generating storms; a uniform interval and final observation date are not established by the summary page. CSV tables and GeoJSON are available through EDI under CC0-1.0 at no cost. The portal presented a human-verification check before its metadata became readable. Monitoring locations changed over time, and some SNAZ observations are maintained in a separate package. Simulation uses include calibrating urban runoff and water-quality models and testing how green infrastructure changes downstream transport. The package complements data-international-stormwater-bmp-database with detailed local observations. It does not represent every drainage installation or storm in metropolitan Phoenix.
